sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: specifier_set_to_range
tools.description:
Convert a specifier set to a version range that represents the same versions.
    
    Args:
        specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        A string representation of the equivalent version range
        
    Example:
        >>> specifier_set_to_range(">=1.0,<2.0")
        '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'

tools.name: specifier_set_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained within a specifier set using the 'in' operator. version: A version string to check against the specifier set, e.g. '3.1.0' -> true. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers (e.g., '>=3.0,!=3.1')

tools.name: version_range_full
tools.description: Create a version range that accepts all possible PEP 440 versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary version strings; prereleases: whether to include pre-release versions. Example: version_range_full() -> '<VersionRange '(-inf, +inf)' arbitrary>'

tools.name: filter_version_range
tools.description:
Yield items from iterable whose version falls inside the range defined by specifiers.
    
    Args:
        specifiers: A string representing version specifiers (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        iterable: An iterable of version strings
        prereleases: Whether to include pre-releases; None uses PEP 440 default behavior
        
    Returns:
        List of version strings from iterable that fall within the specified range
        
    Example:
        >>> filter_version_range(">=1.0,<2.0", ["0.9", "1.5", "2.0"])
        ['1.5']

tools.name: is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether a specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    A specifier set is unsatisfiable if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously
        
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: is_version_range_empty
tools.description: Check if a version range accepts no versions at all. specifier_set: A specifier set string that defines the version range, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> False. prereleases: Whether pre-releases should be included in the range.

tools.name: specifier_contains
tools.description: Return whether a specific version is contained in a specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'. version: The version string to check for containment in the specifier. prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440. >>> specifier_contains('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: filter_specifier
tools.description:
Filter items in the given iterable, that match the specifier.
    
    :param specifier: A version specifier string
    :param iterable: An iterable of version strings or Version instances
    :param prereleases: Whether to include prereleases in the results
    
    >>> list(Specifier(">=1.2.3").filter(["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"]))
    ['1.3']

tools.name: specifier_set_check_contains
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained in a specifier set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set: A string representation of the specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1')
        version: The version string to check for containment in the specifier set
        prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. 
                     If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.
        installed: Whether or not the item is installed. If set to True, it will accept 
                   prerelease versions even if the specifier does not allow them.
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the version is contained in the specifier set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> specifier_set_check_contains('>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1', '1.2.3')
        True

tools.name: specifier_equal
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Specifier objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Specifier object.
    
    Example: specifier_equal(">=1.0", ">=1.0") -> True

tools.name: specifier_set_equal
tools.description:
The `==` operator with SpecifierSet objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a SpecifierSet object.
    
    Example: specifier_set_equal(">=3.0,!=3.1", ">=3.0,!=3.1") -> True

tools.name: specifier_set_intersection
tools.description: Find the intersection of two specifier sets using the '&' operator. left: A string representation of the left specifier set, right: A string representation of the right specifier set. Example: specifier_set_intersection('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=1.5,<2.5') -> '>=1.5,<2.0'.

tools.name: version_range_empty
tools.description: Create an empty version range that accepts no versions. prereleases: whether pre-release versions should be considered. -> string representation of the empty version range.

tools.name: version_range_singleton
tools.description: Return the strict singleton range `{version}`. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '{1.0}'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: canonicalize_version
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version as a string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=False -> '1.0.0'.

tools.name: version_range_complement
tools.description:
Get a version range that contains all versions not in the original range.
    
    Args:
        version_specifier: A version specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0', '<2.0', '==1.5')
        
    Returns:
        A string representation of the complement version range
        
    Example:
        >>> version_range_complement('>=1.0')
        '<1.0'

tools.name: canonicalize_package_name
tools.description: Normalize a Python package or extra name to its canonical form. name: The name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonicalize_package_name('Django') 'django'

tools.name: version_range_union_method
tools.description:
Create a union of two version ranges containing all versions from both.
    
    Args:
        version_range_a (str): First version range in string format
        version_range_b (str): Second version range in string format
    
    Returns:
        str: A string representation of the union of the two version ranges
    
    Example:
        >>> version_range_union_method(">=1.0,<2.0", ">=2.0,<3.0")
        '>=1.0,<3.0'

tools.name: version_range_difference
tools.description:
Compute the difference between two version ranges (versions in first but not second).
    
    Args:
        first_range (str): The first version range specifier
        second_range (str): The second version range specifier to subtract from the first
    
    Returns:
        str: A string representation of the resulting version range
    
    Example:
        >>> version_range_difference(">=1.0", ">=2.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: is_version_range_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two version ranges have no overlapping versions.
    
    Args:
        range1 (str): A version range specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        range2 (str): Another version range specifier string (e.g., '>=2.0,<3.0')
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the ranges are disjoint (no overlap), False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> is_version_range_disjoint('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=2.0,<3.0')
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_subset
tools.description:
Check if every version matching this set also matches another set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set: A string representation of the first specifier set
        other_set: A string representation of the second specifier set to check against
    
    Returns:
        True if every version matching the first set also matches the second set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_subset(">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two specifier sets share no matching versions.
    
    Args:
        specifiers1 (str): A string of version specifiers for the first set
        specifiers2 (str): A string of version specifiers for the second set
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the sets share no matching versions, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_disjoint("<3.12", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: is_normalized_package_name
tools.description: Check if a name is already in its normalized form. name: The project name to check for normalization -> true if the name is normalized, false otherwise.

tools.name: normalize_pre_release
tools.description: Normalize the pre-release segment of a version string. letter: The pre-release identifier to normalize, e.g. 'alpha' -> 'a'.

tools.name: is_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if every version in another range is also in this range. range1: A version range specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: Another version range specifier string to check if it's a subset of range1. Example: is_version_range_superset('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=1.5,<1.8') -> True.

tools.name: version_range_check_contains
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained in a version range.
    
    :param range_spec: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
    :param version: The version string to check against the range
    :return: True if the version is contained in the range, False otherwise
    
    >>> version_range_check_contains(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5")
    True
    >>> version_range_check_contains(">=1.0,<2.0", "2.0")
    False

tools.name: is_specifier_set_superset
tools.description:
Return whether every version matching other also matches this set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): A string representation of the main specifier set
        other_set (str): A string representation of the other specifier set to check against
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if every version matching other also matches this set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_superset(">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.13")
        True

tools.name: parse_version
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the :class:`Version` constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: version_equal
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Version objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example:
    >>> version_equal("1.0a5", "1.0")
    False

tools.name: version_less_than
tools.description:
The `<` operator with Version objects, as in `left < right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `<`, never as a call of `__lt__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example: version_less_than("1.0a5", "1.0") -> True

tools.name: version_less_equal
tools.description:
The `<=` operator with Version objects, as in `left <= right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `<=`, never as a call of `__le__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example:
    >>> version_less_equal("1.0a5", "1.0")
    True

tools.name: version_greater_than
tools.description:
The `>` operator with Version objects, as in `left > right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `>`, never as a call of `__gt__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example: version_greater_than("2.0", "1.5") -> True

tools.name: version_greater_equal
tools.description:
The `>=` operator with Version objects, as in `left >= right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `>=`, never as a call of `__ge__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example:
    >>> version_greater_equal("1.0a5", "1.0")
    False
